value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Additional root cause verified in current GitHub documentation: workflow_dispatch job checks are excluded from PR evaluation and cannot satisfy required branch-rule checks, even when green on the head SHA. This explains the REST-versus-PR-checks discrepancy. Implement the documented GitHub App path: optional client ID plus private-key secret, mint a current-repository token only after local gates, use it for publication and refresh to trigger eligible native pull_request runs, and retain default GITHUB_TOKEN with an explicit setup notice. Native protections remain enforced; no copied or synthetic green statuses. App-enabled maintenance must end inside the one-hour token lifetime. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks and https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Final design adds the documented optional App path because manual head checks are ineligible for PR branch rules. The pinned official token action requests only the caller repository and five explicit permissions (contents/pull-requests/actions write; checks/statuses read), with job-end revocation. Key material is supplied only after caller scripts and local gates. Publication and refresh use the App token to trigger eligible native PR runs; empty config retains GITHUB_TOKEN with a notice, and partial config fails. A forty-minute absolute deadline starts immediately after minting so publication delay counts against token lifetime. App-focused regressions pass 8/8, and the complete focused suite passes 21/21. Rollout follow-up is enriched in existing pm-github-aiok; no caller operations were performed.
